conclusions.formula: s -> lambda_r(Gamma_n,T(t)(s)) is Lebesgue integrable on [0,T].
conclusions.meaning: Integration uses the explicit prescribed piecewise harmonic path on its physical-time interval.
Finite partition includes the final survival arc; differences at finitely many event endpoints are measure zero.

conclusions.formula: lim_(s upward to t_j, s in [0,T]) Gamma(t)(s) = a_j := Phi_(t_j-t_(j-1))(z_(j-1)), for 1<=j<=n.
conclusions.meaning: a_j is the pre-jump phase; Gamma(t)(t_j)=z_j is post-jump. Thus source rate lambda(Gamma(t)(t_j-)) equals lambda(a_j).

conclusions.formula: rho_n,T(t) = ofReal(exp(-integral_0^T lambda_r(Gamma(t)(s)) ds) * product_(j=1)^n lambda_r(Gamma(t)(t_j-))).
conclusions.meaning: All incoming rates are nonnegative, so ofReal product identities are valid. No conditional normalization appears.

path_conventions: Gamma is defined on closed [0,T], post-bounce at internal event instants.
The last arc includes T for path evaluation; endpoint inclusion does not alter a Lebesgue integral.

State the left limit within [0,T]; do not introduce an unspecified extension outside that interval. Any chosen total extension needs explicit agreement and extension-independence at interior jump times.
No left limit is demanded at initial time0 or at nonexistent jumps.
Zero-normal reflection remains identity; bounce continuity is unnecessary and must not be assumed.
